meanings.note: plain first-person singular pronoun, used with peers, juniors, or polite -요 endings in casual settings

examples.trans: I'm going to go home.
I saw that movie too.

meanings.note: interrogative adverb asking about manner, state, or outcome

examples.trans: How do you do this?
How did the result turn out?

되다.gloss: to become, to turn out, to happen

meanings.note: indicates a change of state or outcome

meanings.en: to work out, to be okay
meanings.note: used when something functions or is permitted

examples.trans: Do you have time tomorrow?
Everything is ready.

날아가다.gloss: to fly away; (slang) to get fired or axed

meanings.note: literal movement through the air away from the speaker

meanings.en: to get fired, to lose one's post
meanings.note: colloquial workplace slang for being dismissed or having a job/project cancelled

examples.trans: The bird flew away into the sky.
Is my position going to get axed this time too?

meanings.note: second-person singular pronoun used with close friends or juniors

examples.trans: Are you busy today?
Don't you worry.

meanings.note: placed directly before a verb or adjective to negate it

examples.trans: It's not raining today.
I haven't eaten lunch yet.

meanings.en: first of all, for starters, for the time being
meanings.note: marks an immediate first step before dealing with anything else

examples.trans: Let's sit down and talk first.
Let's wait until today for now.

meanings.note: loanword from English 'member', commonly used for regular cast members of variety shows or teams

examples.trans: A new member joined.
All our team members gathered.

meanings.note: indicates doing or making something again from scratch

examples.trans: I made a new plan.
A new cafe opened here.

짜다.gloss: to put together, to organize, to plan

meanings.en: to put together, to organize, to draw up
meanings.note: used for assembling a team, schedule, or plan
literal meaning of pressing liquid out

examples.trans: I planned the travel schedule in advance.
We need to reorganize the team.

meanings.note: repeating an action or returning to a previous state

examples.trans: Please say that one more time.
I'll come back in a moment.

들어가보다.gloss: to try going in, to step back in

meanings.en: to try going in, to enter and see
meanings.note: compound of 들어가다 (to go in) + -아/어 보다 (to try doing)

examples.trans: Let's try going inside first.
I decided to jump into the new project.

meanings.note: spoken words or remarks
used in ...란 말이야 to emphasize or clarify a statement

examples.trans: I understand what you mean.
Listen to what I'm saying.

meanings.note: interrogative noun asking about time; combines with particles like -부터 (from)

examples.trans: When did you come to Korea?
Since when have you worked here?

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: refers to the present moment

examples.trans: Let's leave right now.
What time is it now?

meanings.en: immediately, on the spot, right this second
meanings.note: often paired with 지금 (지금 당장) for strong emphasis

examples.trans: Try calling right away.
We have to start right this second.

meanings.note: superlative adverb placed before adjectives or verbs

examples.trans: What food do you like the most?
Health is the most important thing.

급하다.gloss: to be urgent, to be in a hurry

meanings.note: describes a matter that needs immediate attention
describes a person's temperament

examples.trans: Something urgent came up.
Don't rush your thinking too much.

meanings.note: bound noun requiring a preceding modifier; often shortened to 거 in speech

examples.trans: Whose is this?
What's important right now is time.

meanings.note: adverbial form of 빠르다 (to be fast)

examples.trans: Please get ready quickly.
Time goes by so fast.

알리다.gloss: to inform, to notify, to let know

meanings.en: to inform, to notify, to announce
meanings.note: causative form of 알다 (to know)

examples.trans: I shared the news with my friends.
Please let me know when you arrive.

meanings.note: refers both to broadcasting in general and to a specific show

examples.trans: A new show starts tonight.
All preparations for the broadcast are finished.

meanings.note: used both transitively and intransitively

examples.trans: The meeting is starting soon.
I started studying Korean.

meanings.note: used in -(으)ㄹ 때 to mean 'when (doing something)'

examples.trans: I'll call you when I go home.
I lived in Seoul when I was young.

보다.gloss: to see, to look, to watch

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: basic perception verb; -(으)면 보면 means 'when you look at it'
auxiliary verb after -아/어

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
If you look closely, it's different.

meanings.note: traditional Korean celebration marking a baby's first birthday, full of guests and festivities

examples.trans: I'm going to my friend's baby's first-birthday party this weekend.
Many guests came to the first-birthday party.

같다.gloss: to be like, to seem like, to be the same

meanings.en: to be like, to look/feel like
meanings.note: follows a noun directly (N 같다) to express resemblance
indicates identity or equality

examples.trans: The weather today feels like spring.
Our thoughts are the same.

meanings.note: used in 막을 내리다 / 막 내리다 ('to bring down the curtain', i.e., to end a show or era)

examples.trans: The performance came to an end.
The stage curtain went up.

내리다.gloss: to lower, to come down, to get off

meanings.note: used in 막 내리다 (to bring down the curtain / end a show)

meanings.en: to come down, to fall; to get off
meanings.note: used for rain/snow falling or getting off transit

examples.trans: I'm getting off at the next station.
It is snowing outside.

meanings.note: a house or venue where a funeral/wake is being held; often used figuratively for a gloomy, deserted place

examples.trans: The atmosphere feels completely like a funeral home.
I went to a funeral wake last evening.

meanings.note: common in farewells like 또 만나요! (See you again!)

examples.trans: See you again next time!
It started raining again.

meanings.note: used for meeting people or in farewells (또 만나요)

examples.trans: Let's meet at the cafe tomorrow.
I met a friend for the first time in a while.
